newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent per lb weaker on Thursday, based on market orders at 1016 EDT, dealers said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture put new sales for the week ended May 29 at 56,300 480-lb bales for the 1997/98 crop, and at 90,200 bales for the current crop.
The largest sales was made to Turkey, which bought 160,000 bales of cotton during the week.
Market sources do not expect the numbers to nudge the market out of its current trading range between 73.00 cents, and resistance at 74.10 cents basis July, where buy stops have been cited.
Wednesday, July cotton settled 0.30 cent lower at 73.12 cents per pound, traded 73.45 to 73.00 cents. New crop December went out 0.11 cent weaker at 75.65 cents.
Volume was estimated at a thin 8,500 lots.
